h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר ב׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Bais

p: Beis is the two arms, Gedulah and Gevurah;
In it, Shabbos is equal to the entire Torah:
תְּלַת כִּתְרִין דְּש' — תְּלַת סְפִירִין עִילָּאִין וְכוּלֵּי.
the three crowns of the Shin are the three supernal Sefiros, etc."
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar
בַּת מִתְעַטְּרָא בְּאֲבָהָן, ש' רָזָא דִּתְלַת אֲבָהָן.
"The Daughter is crowned with the Fathers; Shin is the secret of the three Patriarchs."
And in another place in the holy Zohar
שְׁכִינְתָּא אִתְקְרִיאַת שַׁבָּת מִסִּטְרָא דִּתְלַת דַּרְגִּין עִילָּאִין:
"The Shechinah is called Shabbos from the aspect of the three supernal levels:
ש' תְּלַת כִּתְרִין: כֶּתֶר חָכְמָה בִּינָה,
Shin is three crowns: Kesser, Chochmah, Binah,
and she is Bas, the fourth to them."
וְכָאן חָשַׁב בַּת חֶסֶד גְּבוּרָה תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁהָאָבוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה לָהֶם,
Whereas here (in Tikkun 19) it counted Bas as Chessed, Gevurah, Tiferes, for which the Patriarchs are chariots,
שֶׁהָאָבוֹת מִתְעַטְּרִין בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וּמַשְׁפִּיעִין קְדוּשָּׁתָם לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל:
because the Patriarchs are crowned with the first three Sefiros and bestow their holiness upon Knesses Yisrael:
"The Daughter is crowned with the Fathers."
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא דְּבַת רְבִיעָאָה לוֹן,
And this is what they said in Ra'aya Mehemna, that Bas is the fourth to them,
רַק שָׁם חָשַׁב הַש' הָאָבוֹת וּבַת נְקוּדָּה עִילָּאָה
only there it counted the Shin as the Patriarchs and Bas as the supernal point
"Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem"
that he repents while he is a man in his prime;
"and his heart will understand (yavin) and repent,"
for Binah is the supernal repentance.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה כִּזְכוּיוֹת שֶׁמְּבָרֵר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,
That is, intentional sins become like merits, which Hashem, may He be blessed, clarifies,
שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה בְּמַאֲמָר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהוּזְכַּר בּוֹ תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ וְחֹשֶׁךְ
for so it was in the first utterance of Creation, where "tohu vavohu and darkness" were mentioned,
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
which alludes to the deeds of the wicked, as stated in the Midrash
וְהַיְינוּ דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא,
and that is because "there is no light except that which emerges from darkness,"
as brought in the holy Zohar
And then they become like merits, and as they said
אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית
"If your sins be like these years that stand ordered and coming from the six days of Creation,
then they shall become white as snow."
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן בָּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this too comes through fear, and as it is said
"Then you will understand (tavin) the fear of Hashem"
when fear enters the depths of the heart.
וְזֶהוּ שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל עַד מַאֲמָר בְּרֵאשִׁית,
And this is Shabbos HaGadol reaching up to the utterance of "Bereishis,"
וְהוּא הַדַּעַת, שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים מֵחֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה.
which is Da'as, the fiftieth gate of the fifty gates of Binah.
And this is revealed only to penitents,
this refers to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues:
דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא נִגְלוּ לְמֹשֶׁה נִגְלוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְכוּלֵּי.
things that were not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva, etc.
שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא יָדַע מֵרַע כְּלָל וְלֹא קִלְקֵל מֵעוֹלָם,
For Moshe Rabbeinu knew nothing of evil at all and never sinned,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁאָמַר: כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי עַם הָאָרֶץ
unlike Rabbi Akiva, who said, "When I was an unlearned person"
לוֹ נִגְלָה שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁהוּא כָּל יְקָר
to him was revealed the fiftieth gate, which is "every precious thing"
"More precious than wisdom is a little folly"
meaning the light that emerges from darkness.
And this is called Shabbos HaGadol:
הַחֵשֶׁק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה,
the yearning for words of Torah, which is supernal repentance,
דְּאַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה יַעֲסוֹק בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ.
that after repentance one engages in Torah with fear and love.
וְכֵן הָיָה יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
And so was the Exodus from Egypt, which through the attribute of Chessed was a preparation for the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן הָאַהֲבָה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע.
which was also love from Israel's side, as they preceded "we will do" to "we will hear."
וְשַׁבָּת הַקָּטָן יִרְאָה, שֶׁנִּקְרָא גַּם כֵּן לֵב,
And Shabbos HaKatan is fear, which is also called "heart,"
"וְלֶב אָיִן" — שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ תּוֹרָה וְאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
"'And he has no heart'—one who has Torah but does not have fear of Heaven."
תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה בָּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
Lower repentance also comes through fear, as we have said.
And on Shabbos, when one merits the revelation of Atika,
זוֹכִין לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה שֶׁהוּא בָּא מִיִּרְאָה עִילָּאָה,
one merits the Supernal Shabbos, which comes from supernal fear
וְאוֹמְרִים "נְהוֹרֵיהּ יִשְׁרֵי בַּהּ" עַל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה וְעִילָּאָה,
And we say "May His light rest upon it" regarding the words of Torah merited through lower and supernal repentance,
"It is good to give thanks (and confess) to Hashem,"
"He who confesses and forsakes [his sins] will obtain mercy."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 19 (40b) — "Shin: Shabbos HaGadol, Binah; Shabbos HaKatan, Malchus. Beis: the two arms, Gedulah and Gevurah. Tav: Tiferes. Through it Shabbos is equal to the whole Torah. The three crowns of the Shin are the three supernal Sefiros, and all are included in teshuvah, which is the upper Shechinah."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Maamarei Chodesh Nisan, Maamar 3:4 — “There is repentance and there is repentance. There is repentance from fear: one regrets his past sins and turns from evil out of awe of his Maker, and through it intentional sins become like unintentional ones; yet even the unintentional needs atonement, for its mark is still visible. But when after this he rises to repentance from love, to engage in the mitzvos in the aspect of ‘do good,’ intentional sins become like merits. Lower repentance and fear are the final Hei, the awe of Malchus; supernal repentance, from love, is the first Hei, Binah, Shabbos HaGadol, the supernal Jubilee that brings a person out to freedom, and from there comes the salvation of redemption.” Connection: Both identify Shabbos HaGadol with Binah and supernal repentance, through which sins become merits, set against a lower repentance of fear; Bnei Yissaschar adds that the lower kind still leaves a mark, which only repentance from love erases.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Shabbos HaGadol 5634 — “In every Shabbos there is an aspect of the Exodus, as it says, ‘a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,’ and the Zohar says the Exodus is mentioned fifty times in the Torah, for all the gates of Binah have their Egypt. Even the smallest point of understanding has fifty gates, and on each Shabbos one gate is opened. Shabbos HaGadol is also like Shabbos Teshuvah, except that it is in the aspect of love: every person must return to Hashem out of the greatness of the kindness He did in bringing us out of Egypt. Since the fiftieth gate is the root of freedom, the wicked could not stand against it, and the Holy One redeemed us before we entered the fiftieth gate of impurity; therefore this gate is called Shabbos HaGadol.” Connection: Both link Shabbos HaGadol to repentance and to the fiftieth gate of Binah; Sefas Emes adds that it is a repentance drawn from love for the kindness of the Exodus.

He said: This one bites and breaks the bone; that one bites and does not break the bone." Rashi has no comment on this line.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 1 — “In ‘Bereishis’ darkness comes first and afterwards ‘Let there be light,’ for there is no light except what comes out of darkness. Rabbi Akiva needed this, for through it he reached his level: ‘His eye saw every precious thing’ — things not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva. That is the fiftieth gate, given over to the baal teshuvah and not revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu, who never sinned. Not so Rabbi Akiva, who said, ‘When I was an am ha'aretz.’ Therefore he merited the fiftieth gate, and he merited it by yearning all his days to sanctify the Name: ‘When will it come to my hand, that I may fulfill it?’” Connection: Both give Rabbi Akiva the fiftieth gate as light out of darkness; Toldos 1 reads “thus it arose in thought” about his death this way and names his lifelong yearning for martyrdom as how he reached it.

He merits the letter Vav, the son of Yah, after whom Binah is named; he causes the Vav to return to the Hei — teshuvah: tashuv Vav la-Hei."

— "There is a person who, after regretting his sins and doing teshuvah, engages in Torah in fear and love of the Holy One, not in order to receive reward. He merits the letter Vav, the son of Yah, after whom Binah is named; he causes the Vav to return to the Hei — teshuvah: tashuv Vav la-Hei."

Woe to the enemies of Torah scholars [a euphemism for the scholars themselves] who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven." Rashi has no comment on this line.
